tag.name: GA4 - Ecommerce Event - Supported Events
tag.notes:
# Purpose:
Sends supported GA4 ecommerce events through one shared GA4 Event tag.

The GA4 event name is taken dynamically from the GTM built-in {{Event}} variable.

# Use:
Used to send the following ecommerce events to GA4:

- `add_payment_info`
- `add_shipping_info`
- `add_to_cart`
- `add_to_wishlist`
- `begin_checkout`
- `purchase`
- `remove_from_cart`
- `select_item`
- `select_promotion`
- `view_cart`
- `view_item`
- `view_item_list`
- `view_promotion`

# Trigger conditions:
Fires when one of the assigned ecommerce Custom Event triggers is received.

# Expected data:
A valid GA4 ecommerce object matching the incoming event.

Common parameters include:

- currency
- value
- items

Event-specific parameters may include:

- `add_payment_info` → payment_type
- `add_shipping_info` → shipping_tier
- `purchase` → transaction_id, tax, shipping, affiliation, coupon
- `select_item` → item_list_id, item_list_name
- `view_item_list` → item_list_id, item_list_name
- `select_promotion` → promotion_id, promotion_name, creative_name, creative_slot
- `view_promotion` → promotion_id, promotion_name, creative_name, creative_slot

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "add_to_cart",
  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 29.90,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 1
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Uses {{Event}} as the GA4 event name.
- Sends ecommerce data directly from the `ecommerce` object in the Data Layer.
- Fires only for the Custom Event triggers assigned to this tag.
- Do not create separate GA4 tags for the same events, as this can cause duplicate events.
- Each event must include the parameters expected for that event.
- Clear the previous ecommerce object before each ecommerce event when old data could remain in the Data Layer.
- `add_to_cart` and `remove_from_cart` should reflect completed cart changes, not button clicks alone.
- `add_to_wishlist` should fire only after the product has been added successfully.
- `begin_checkout` should fire when the checkout process starts.
- `add_shipping_info` should fire after the shipping method is confirmed.
- `add_payment_info` should fire after the payment method is confirmed.
- `view_item_list` and `view_promotion` should fire when the content is actually shown to the user.
- `select_item` and `select_promotion` should fire from confirmed user interactions.
- `purchase` must fire only once per transaction.
- `transaction_id` must be unique and must not contain any PII.
- Consider storage-based purchase deduplication using `transaction_id`.
- Validate every supported event in GTM Preview and GA4 DebugView before publishing.

trigger.name: Custom Event - View Item (Product Page)
Custom Event - View Cart
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when the user views the cart.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `view_cart` events to track cart visibility and user intent before checkout.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "view_cart"

# Expected data:
ecommerce.items array representing current cart contents

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "view_cart",
  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 59.80,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 2
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire when the cart page or cart view is loaded.
- Should reflect the current state of the cart at the time of viewing.
- Avoid firing on minor UI updates (e.g. quantity changes) unless the cart is fully re-rendered.
- Ensure items array matches the actual cart contents.
- Consider deduplication if the cart page can reload or be revisited.

trigger.name: Custom Event - Begin Checkout
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when checkout process starts.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `begin_checkout` events.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "begin_checkout"

# Expected data:
Full cart items

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "begin_checkout",
  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 59.80,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 2
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
Should fire once when entering checkout.
Avoid duplicates on reload.

trigger.name: Custom Event - Add Payment Info
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when payment method is added.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `add_payment_info` events.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "add_payment_info"

# Expected data:
Payment type and items

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "add_payment_info",
  ecommerce: {
    payment_type: "credit_card",
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 59.80,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 2
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
Should fire after user confirms payment method.

trigger.name: Custom Event - Purchase (Order/Transaction Completed)
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when a transaction is completed.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `purchase` events.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "purchase"

# Expected data:
Full ecommerce object including transaction_id

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "purchase",
  ecommerce: {
    transaction_id: "ORDER-100245",
    value: 64.70,
    currency: "EUR",
    tax: 4.90,
    shipping: 5.00,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 2
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
Must fire only once per transaction.
transaction_id is used for deduplication.

trigger.name: Custom Event - Add to Cart
Custom Event - Add Shipping Info
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when shipping method is selected.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `add_shipping_info` events.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "add_shipping_info"

# Expected data:
Shipping tier and items

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "add_shipping_info",
  ecommerce: {
    shipping_tier: "Express",
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 59.80,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 2
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
Should fire after shipping selection.

Custom Event - Select Item
Custom Event - Add to Wishlist
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when a user adds a product to their wishlist.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `add_to_wishlist` events to track product interest outside of the purchase funnel.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "add_to_wishlist"

# Expected data:
ecommerce.items array with the selected product

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "add_to_wishlist",
  ecommerce: {
    currency: "EUR",
    value: 29.90,
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        quantity: 1
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire only when a product is actually added to the wishlist.
- Should not fire on page load or when viewing wishlist items.
- Ensure items array contains accurate product data.

trigger.name: Custom Event - View Item List
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when a product list is viewed.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `view_item_list` events for product list impressions.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "view_item_list"

# Expected data:
ecommerce.items array with list context

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "view_item_list",
  ecommerce: {
    item_list_name: "Search Results",
    item_list_id: "search_results",
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90,
        item_list_name: "Search Results",
        index: 1
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
Should fire once per list view.
Ensure list metadata is included for attribution.

trigger.name: Custom Event - Select Promotion
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when a user clicks or selects a promotion.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `select_promotion` events to measure engagement with internal promotions (e.g. banners, hero sections, campaign blocks).

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "select_promotion"

# Expected data:
- promotion_id → String
- promotion_name → String
- creative_name → String
- creative_slot → String
- items → Array (optional, if tied to products)

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "select_promotion",
  ecommerce: {
    promotion_id: "summer_sale_2025",
    promotion_name: "Summer Sale",
    creative_name: "Homepage Banner v1",
    creative_slot: "homepage_top",
    items: [...]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire when a user clicks or interacts with a promotion.
- Should not fire on promotion visibility (use `view_promotion` for impressions).
- Ensure promotion_id remains consistent across all related events.
- Use together with promotion_name, creative_name, and creative_slot for full attribution.
- Consider deduplication if multiple clicks can fire rapidly.

trigger.name: Custom Event - View Promotion
trigger.notes:
# Purpose:
Triggers when a promotion is viewed by the user.

# Use:
Used to fire GA4 `view_promotion` events to measure promotion impressions.

# Trigger conditions:
Event equals "view_promotion"

# Expected data:
- promotion_id → String
- promotion_name → String
- creative_name → String
- creative_slot → String
- items → Array (optional, if tied to products)

Example:
dataLayer.push({
  event: "view_promotion",
  ecommerce: {
    promotion_id: "summer_sale_2025",
    promotion_name: "Summer Sale",
    creative_name: "Homepage Banner v1",
    creative_slot: "homepage_top",
    items: [
      {
        item_id: "SKU123",
        item_name: "Blue T-Shirt",
        price: 29.90
      }
    ]
  }
});

# Notes:
- Should fire when the promotion is visible to the user (e.g. on page load or when scrolled into view).
- Should not fire on user interaction (use `select_promotion` for clicks).
- Ensure promotion_id remains consistent across view_promotion and select_promotion events.
- Use together with promotion_name, creative_name, and creative_slot for full attribution.
- Consider deduplication if promotions can re-render or appear multiple times during the session.

variable.name: CJS - Same page referrer
variable.notes:
Detects if the current page load was caused by a browser refresh (reload).

Why this matters:
* Some setups (e.g. WordPress, plugins, or AJAX flows) can trigger duplicate events when the page reloads. This function helps you identify that case so you can block duplicate GTM tags.
